entries.topic: Media, public campaigns and information, both sides, added to the network map (Nov 2026)

claims.text: Truman wrote that he never faced as much pressure and propaganda aimed at the White House as over Palestine.

Truman told Senator Pepper on 17 October 1947 that he had received about 35,000 pieces of mail on Palestine; Wallace recorded a sheaf of telegrams about four inches thick in July 1946; a late-1947 poll found 65% of Americans in favour of partition; Loy Henderson judged that the Zionists had Congress, the press and most Americans.

We Will Never Die: Madison Square Garden 9 March 1943, then Washington, Philadelphia, Chicago, Boston and the Hollywood Bowl; at least 100,000 in all; in Washington more than 200 members of Congress, seven justices and Eleanor Roosevelt; written by Ben Hecht for the Bergson group's Committee for a Jewish Army; its aim was rescue.
JTA founded by Jacob Landau in The Hague on 6 February 1917; London 1919; New York 1922; more than 400 subscribing newspapers by 1925.
Gershon Agron: Zionist Commission press office 1920-21; JTA editor 1921-24; founded the Palestine Post in 1932; headed Israel's information service 1949-51.

Renton and Friedman argue that propaganda aimed at Jewish opinion in the United States and Russia was a main motive for the Balfour Declaration; a disputed claim about motive, recorded without weight.
The Arab Office, directed by Musa Alami, presented the Arab case to the Anglo-American Committee in 1946, led by Albert Hourani, with more than a thousand pages of documentation.
